alternatives.root_cause: frontend's process was stopped while its listening socket stayed open, so callers hung to their deadlines.
alternatives.why_not: A freeze stalls every request, but frontend served POST /api/cart end-to-end in milliseconds, with full downstream child spans, moments after a 15s hang in the same trace (tr_c58f11300073).

alternatives.root_cause: A dependency of frontend became slow and frontend failed because it waited.
alternatives.why_not: The hanging frontend spans have no child spans at all and carry the full duration as self-time; cart, product-catalog and flagd all respond in milliseconds throughout the window (tr_954fe70d5995, tr_c58f11300073).

alternatives.root_cause: frontend-proxy was misconfigured with a wrong upstream or timeout and stalled requests itself.
alternatives.why_not: The proxy's own self-time is sub-millisecond and it correctly propagates to a live frontend span; no change was recorded for it in a 24h window (tr_aae08a0ffa3a, tr_60ac92d34ea9).

alternatives.root_cause: frontend exhausted its request-handling threads or connections, queueing requests until deadline.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible as a downstream effect, but nothing observed shows a saturation signal, and interleaved fast successes argue the handler pool was not uniformly starved; no supporting metric or log was obtainable.

verdict.summary: A runtime-flagged code path in frontend began hanging on certain page/API GET requests, holding each request with no downstream work until callers hit their 15s deadline, while no artifact or configuration change was recorded anywhere.
verdict.reasoning: frontend-proxy and load-generator alert, but their failing spans are pure waits on the frontend hop: the frontend span consumes essentially the whole 15s as self-time and emits no child spans, so the stall is inside frontend before it calls any dependency (tr_954fe70d5995, tr_c58f11300073). Downstream services (cart, product-catalog, flagd) continue to answer in single-digit milliseconds in the same traces, so no dependency became slow. frontend's own error ratio stays flat at zero while the proxy's rises 37x with a change point just before onset (tr_7c9375e06efa, tr_66657ef96618) - the signature of a service that hangs rather than fails, with the error surfacing only at the caller. Within one trace a hanging GET is followed by a POST that frontend serves normally in milliseconds (tr_c58f11300073), so the process is alive, accepting and executing work; that excludes a frozen or partitioned process, which would stall everything. No deploy or configuration change exists for frontend or frontend-proxy over a 24h window (tr_9ee7bf2366fc, tr_aae08a0ffa3a), and none for the flag service either (tr_af7db258e33c), which is exactly the empty change log expected when the trigger is a runtime flag flip rather than an artifact or file edit. Remediation is to revert the flag value in the flag store.
open_questions: Which flag and which code path: the log backend returned nothing for any service queried, so no frontend-side statement of what it was doing during the stall was obtainable.
Why only some request paths hang while others succeed - whether the selection is by route, by flag sampling percentage, or by a saturated worker pool.
Whether a worker/connection pool in frontend is being exhausted by the stuck requests as a secondary effect, which would be an alternative mechanism for the same symptom.
The exact flip time in the flag store; onset was inferred from the proxy error-ratio change point, not from a flag audit record.
